Commentary.Commentary: That's it from this game then! Pakistan have stunned themselves more than anyone by choking so badly. Can they recover from this in 4 days' time? The second Test will be played in Dubai, from Saturday, November 24, 2018 at 10 am local (0600 GMT). ADIOS! TAKE CARE!

Kane Williamson says that the team knew that the surface wasn't the easiest to bat on and a lot of scrappy batting was required. Observes that plenty of turn was available from even Day 1 and is happy to have come out on the right side of the result. Admits that there are a few batting issues to be resolved but then praises the effort put in. Has words of praise for the attitude shown, especially during the times when wickets fell in clumps. Praises Ajaz and Sodhi for bowling tirelessly this morning and does not know what might have happened had they not applied the pressure. Agrees that there are plenty of 'little' areas which need to be worked over but in the larger perspective of the game, Williamson says that he is more pleased with the attitude shown.

Pakistan captain Sarfraz Ahmed admits that he is very disappointed. Says that when his side lost 3 quick wickets, it seemed like the match was over but then the Azhar-Shafiq stand revived fortunes. To lose from there, is even more heartbreaking, he adds. Praises Ajaz Patel for his accuracy but then believes his batsmen could have shown more patience. Admits that in the first place, this game should not have gone down to the wire and the batsmen should have played more shots. But when it did, then they should have shown some application. Hopes to learn from these mistakes in the future.

AJAZ PATEL HAS BEEN NAMED THE MAN OF THE MATCH. Says that his game plan was pretty simple. New Zealand believed that they could keep plugging away and thanks the almighty for letting that happen. Credits the relaxed environment in the dressing room for helping the players absorb the pressure and not overdo things. On his debut, he says that he just tried to remind himself of all the hard work that he has done to get to this stage and on his bowling, he says that he just tried to keep it simple.

Ajaz Patel has a chat with Danny Morisson. The former smiles on being given the ball on having got a 5-fer. Says that it is a very special feeling to have done well and led your team to a win. Stresses further that they played the 'Kiwi' way of cricket, not giving up till the last ball. On the words during the Lunch break, Ajaz says that the discussion was just to keep it simple and not give anything away. Adds that it is quite rewarding to win a game for your country after all the hard work he has put in all these years. Stay tuned for the presentation...

The Babar run out seemed to inspire New Zealand and Pakistan both. The bowling side sensed that they can run through the lower order. The batting unit felt that they needed to get things done quickly. Atrocious shots were played, to say the least and only Azhar Ali seemed to be calm under pressure. However, perhaps he could have batted a bit better with the tail - maybe played more shots?

It seemed to be a non-eventful ball. Flicked towards square leg. Could have been a single, would not have mattered even if it was a dot ball. But then, communication was given no respect by either of the two Pakistan batsmen. Babar Azam was admiring the fielding effort while Azhar Ali desperately wanted the single. Neither a yes, nor a no. Just run and watch. What transpired was a run out, that of Babar and the game turned on its head.

One would back the batting side, of course, you would say. But Pakistan, being Pakistan, played just like Pakistan. There is a great degree of mercury rising involved when they play - irrespective of whether they win or lose and today was no less. It all started with a small incident. Really small. Perhaps the phone line was dead. Perhaps there was no network. But why did Azhar Ali not even TRY to call?

There were a few twists this morning, with Pakistan losing three wickets quickly for 8 runs. However, when Azhar Ali and Asad Shafiq got a partnership going, it seemed like the writing was on the wall. Even if Asad Shafiq did get out on the last ball before Lunch - just figure this out - 46 runs needed, 6 wickets in hand and plenty of overs left. Whom would you back?

Coming to the match - not quite sure how and where Pakistan lost the game. They made New Zealand collapse from 111/3 to 153 all out and got a lead of 74 in the first innings. Managed to get a decent lead of 74. Then, just when it seemed like the Kiwis were taking the game away, Pakistan restricted them to 249 in the second dig, taking the last 6 wickets for just 29 runs. And then, they raced to 40, without losing a sweat.

Let us take a breather, folks. What did New Zealand have during the Lunch break? Jubilation for the Kiwis. Heartbreak for Pakistan. This is the first time any team has lost by 4 runs in Test cricket. Lowest margin of defeat for Pakistan. Smallest margin of victory for New Zealand. As my colleague, THEONE, usually says to express his feelings - Wow. Just wow.

OUT! New Zealand win by 4 runs. What a Test match! Azhar Ali looks devastated as the Ball Tracker shows the ball to be hitting the top of middle. The decision will remain and Pakistan have imploded quite spectacularly again! The ball was landing on leg and turns enough to beat the outside edge of Azhar Ali who was ahead to defend this one. It goes on to hit his back leg and the umpire thinks a bit before raising his finger. Pakistan had to review but unfortunately for Azhar, it just wasn't his day. It's been a great innings but just couldn't hold his nerve to cross the line in the end. On the other hand though, credit must go to the visitors who came spitting fire after Lunch! And also to some crazy running between Babar Azam and Azhar Ali which began this downfall. The Black Caps will have to be given a lot of appreciation for their 'never-say-die' attitude.
Azhar has been adjudged LBW! The decision though has been reviewed...
Similar ball and similar shot again, again the run is declined.
Shorter outside off, Ali guides it to deep third man but doesn't run.
Flighted outside off, Azhar is drawn forward to drive it to cover-point but no run taken.
Bowls a bouncer, Abbas does well to duck under it.
Slow bouncer, the batsman plays it towards third man. The batsmen take a run.
HAHA! Azhar tries something different. Length delivery outside off stump, Azhar goes for the scoop but misses it completely and gets beaten. Wagner starts to appeal for the catch but then bails out.
Short of a length delivery, the batsman got a low bounce and he pulls it towards mid-wicket.
Short of a length delivery again, Azhar again pulls it towards square leg.
Short of a length delivery, Azhar pulls it towards mid-wicket.
Sensible batting from Ali, he comes down the wicket and drives to long off to pick up a single and retains strike. Only six required now!
Full ball at the pads, Azhar reverse sweeps it but short third man comes around and stops the single.
Slower through the air, Azhar is half ahead and adjusts well to defend this one after it turns away slightly.
Comes down the wicket and hits this full one to long off. No run taken.
Shorter outside off, cut away to deep point but no run taken.
Full and on middle, Azhar defends it back to the bowler.
Full toss around off stump, Abbas defends off the front foot. Wagner fields and throws it back at the stumps but Abbas never left his crease.
Length delivery outside off stump, the batsman plays the upper cut towards third man. The fielder could not quite get to the ball. The batsmen take a run. 7 more needed now.
Length delivery again on off stump, the batsman defends off the front foot.
Length delivery outside off stump, Azhar cuts it towards point. He does not go for the run again. Had he tried, there were two runs on offer.
Full toss on leg stump, Azhar flicks it towards mid-wicket.
Length delivery on off stump, Azhar drives it towards covers.

Not out! There is absolutely nothing on Ultra-Edge. The ball is a brilliant one though! It lands on middle, grips and turns to beat the outside edge of Abbas who was half ahead in defense. Watling and the close-in fielders go up in a huge appeal as Bruce Oxenford shakes his head. The NZ fielders are convinced and ask Williamson to go upstairs. The replays confirm the original decision and that's a lost review for the Black Caps. Drama! Pakistan are trying to do it one run per over here.
IS THAT THE END OF THE MATCH? Abbas has been given not out on a caught behind appeal. New Zealand have taken the review....
Faster and full yorker length ball outside off, Abbas lets it go.
Takes the single this time. Full and outside off, driven to sweeper cover. 8 required now!
Fuller and outside off, Azhar drives to deep cover.
Flighted well outside off, driven to long off but again declines to take a run.
Looped up on off, pushed to sweeper cover by Azhar but no run taken.
Bowls a bouncer, Abbas does well to duck under it.
Slow yorker on middle stump, the batsman digs it out to cover and takes a single. 9 more needed now. Can Abbas survive?
Length delivery on off stump, the batsman defends off the back foot.
BEATEN! Wide outside off stump, Azhar wanted to go for the cut but gets beaten on this one.
Full outside off stump, Azhar drives it towards covers.
Length delivery on off stump, Azhar gets it off the inner half of the bat.
Loud applause from the sparse crowd! Abbas has managed to keep out the three deliveries. This one is overpitched on middle and Abbas comes half forward to defend it straight back to the bowler.
Flatter one on off again, Abbas goes back in the crease and defends it with a straight bat.
Looped up on off, Abbas defends this one confidently.

This one is flatter and quicker on off stump, Azhar Ali drops it down towards point and wants to come back for two, but they can't pick it up as the sweeper cover fielder is quick to it. Abbas on strike now! 10 required.
Fuller outside off, Azhar drives to deep cover but doesn't take the single.
Almost gone through! Azhar comes down the wicket and yorks himself to this full length delivery. He is able to defend it to cover in the end.
Comes around the wicket and bowls on off stump, Abbas does well to defend it off the back foot.
Wide outside off stump, Abbas lets it go.
Length delivery outside off stump, Azhar guides it to third man. The batsmen cross ends. They need 11 more for victory.
Good length delivery on off stump, the batsman defends off the back foot.
Length delivery outside off stump, the batsman cuts it towards point.
Wide outside off stump, Azhar tries to play that but misses it.
Mohammad Abbas is the last man in.

OUT! Yesterday's hero could be today's villain! Hasan Ali, what have you done? No need for him to play this shot at this moment, the ball was flighted outside off and Hasan's eyes lit up on seeing it. He goes for a huge slog over mid-wicket but fails to connect fully. The ball hits the top half of the bat and goes to Tim Southee, who is on as a substitute fielder in place of Ross Taylor. Really good catch under pressure as the ball was high in the air and would've been a difficult catch in the sun. 12 required now and only 1 wicket left.
The batsman has swept that one through the leg side. The batsmen have run through for a single.

In the air and falls in no-man's land. Azhar Ali lofts it over cover. The ball was on off and spinning away. Really good shot under pressure. Played with a lot of control. 2 runs taken by the batsmen.
Huge appeal but there was an inside edge there. Flatter on middle, Azhar Ali just brings the bat down in time to defend it. Luckily, the ball hits the inside edge and hits him on the pads.
Short and outside off, Azhar cuts it straight to point.
Flighted and on middle, Azhar comes ahead and keeps it out.
BEATEN! Good length delivery outside off stump, Hasan tries to go towards mid-wicket but gets completely beaten on this one.
Bowls a bouncer, Hasan does well to duck under it.
Outside off, flayed through the covers for a single.
Outside off, swinging away, left alone.
FOUR! Hammered away! Length delivery outside off stump, Azhar hits it straight past the bowler for a beautiful boundary. 16 more to win!
Full outside off stump, Azhar drives it towards covers.
Goes for another slog an gets it off the inner half through mid-wicket. They do not run.
Sensible from Hasan Ali. Comes forward and defends.
A wild slog from Ali, he misses.
Comes down the track, Azhar comes down the track and pushes it towards long on for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

Not Out! Azhar and Pakistan breathe a huge sigh of relief. This one was down the leg side and Azhar looks to work it away to fine leg but misses it. Watling fails to gather it properly and the ball rolls off his glove and onto the stumps. They appeal for stumping but the back foot of Azhar is firmly on the ground when the bails fall. The foot does come up slightly but the bails had already fallen by then. The tension in the air is palpable.
Is that the 9th wicket? Watling has appealed for a stumping against Azhar. Referred upstairs...
Short and on off, Hasan is inside the crease and defends.
Outside off and full, Hasan leaves it alone.
Hasan Ali is in at no. 10.

OUT! There's the eighth one! Full one after two short ones and Yasir just prods ahead and looks to play it to cover. It takes the outside edge and Ross Taylor who is between first and second slip keeps low to his left and holds on to a good catch. 21 runs still required! New Zealand look to be taking a grip of this game now. 4 wickets have been lost for just 8 runs.
Bumper outside off, Yasir just sways and lets it go through.
Good length well outside off, Yasir watches it go through to the keeper.
Slightly short of a length on off, Azhar pushes it to sweeper for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
The ball is way outside the off stump, easy leave for the batsman.
Tossed up on middle stump, Yasir defends off the back foot.
Caught behind given out by the umpire. Yasir Shah immediately reviews after consulting his partner. Was it the noise of the bat hitting the ground?

NOT OUT! The bat has hit the ground! Lucky escape for Yasir. Tossed up outside off stump, Yasir goes for the drive but misses it completely and is beaten on this one. Watling catches and appeals and the umpire raises his finger! Yasir consults Azhar and goes for the review. Ultra Edge shows no spike. The bat had hit the ground. Phew!
Yasir Shah joins Azhar Ali in the middle.

OUT! BOWLED! New Zealand are on fire. Bowls straight on middle stump, Bilal goes for the slog sweep but misses it completely and gets bowled. Pakistan lose their seventh wicket. Looks like Azhar Ali is stranded of partners.
Tossed up on middle stump, Bilal defends off the front foot.
On a length outside off again, Azhar lets it go through. Maiden over.
Good length, keeps a bit low on the off pole. Azhar defends on the back foot and gets the under edge that runs to gully.
On a length again and outside off, Azhar leaves it again.
Just short of a good length, Ali wants nothing to do with it as it well outside off.
Similar line again, good pace on this one. Azhar lets it go again. He holds the key here and needs to be patient and wait for the bad balls.
Good length ball angling away after landing on off, Azhar shoulders his arms to it.
Bilal Asif is the new man in at 8.

OUT! The decision is overturned! The game is changing big time. Tossed up on middle stump, Sarfraz goes for the sweep but misses. The ball goes in the air and gets caught by BJ Watling. The umpire shakes his head. New Zealand go for the review. Ultra edge shows a spike when the ball goes past his glove! Sarfraz has to walk back. They still need 22 more to win this match.
Is that LBW? Or is it a catch? It has been given not out. New Zealand reckon Sarfraz is out.
Floated on middle stump, the skipper defends off the back foot.
BEATEN! Drifts away from the batsman, Sarfraz goes for the drive but gets completely beaten on this one.
Tossed up on off stump, the skipper plays it towards point.
Flighted delivery on leg stump, Azhar pushes it towards mid-wicket. The batsmen cross ends.
Tossed up on middle stump, Azhar defends off the front foot.
Short one outside off, Sarfraz plays it safely to point.
Over the wicket to Sarfraz and the ball is short and angling away, the skipper ducks and lets it go.
Short and on middle again, Azhar gets inside the line and pulls it away to deep fine leg for a single.
Around the wicket, short and well outside off, Azhar ducks to let it go.
Slower one outside off, driven well by the captain and he's off the mark immediately. The batsmen come back for three.

TOP EDGE, SAFE! Nearly another wicket. A short ball, Azhar goes for the pull but the bounce gets big on him. He miscues it but the top edge does not carry to Trent Boult running in from long leg. A single taken.
Tossed up outside off stump, Azhar cuts it towards point. The fielder misfields and the batsmen take a run.
Loopy delivery on middle stump, Azhar defends off the front foot.
Sarfraz Ahmed is the next batsman in.

Run-out! Unnecessary from Pakistan. Absolute madness in the middle. The ball is full and at the pads, Azam plays it to short fine leg. Azhar Ali has come charging down and it was his call but Azam was ball-watching and doesn't run through. Azhar passes him and reaches the striker's end first, leaving Azam stranded in the middle. There was no need for this as it could set the cat among the pigeons. The fielder at square leg throws it back to Ajaz who dislodges the bails with his foot by mistake. He then goes on to uproot the stump with the ball in his hand. 29 still required. Do you still think New Zealand have a chance?
Flatter on middle, Azam comes forward and defends it with a straight bat.
Full and pitched on leg, Babar gets his bat in front of his pad as he defends.
Flighted on pads, Babar plays it into the ground on the leg side.
Again short of a length delivery, the batsman pulls it towards mid on. The batsmen get three runs.
Short of a length delivery, Babar pulls it towards mid-wicket. The batsmen get two runs.
Short ball again, the batsman wanted to pull but gets it off his shoulder towards point.
Again a bouncer, the batsman does well to duck under it.
Bowls a bouncer, Babar lets it go.
Full outside off stump, Babar drives it towards covers. The batsmen pick up a couple.

Grip and turn for Ajaz as this ball is pitched on off and beats the outside edge of Azhar who was trying to defend, as it turns away at the last moment. Watling is quick to remove the bails but the foot has come back down by that time.
This one is flatter and quicker on off stump, Azam just drops it down on the off side towards point and picks up a quick single. The point fielder has a shy at the non-striker's end but misses it.
FOUR! Freebie for the new batsman. Short and slow outside off, all the time in the world for Azam to rock back and cut it away to the point boundary. 37 away now.
Good use of the feet here as Azhar comes down the wicket and plays this ball which was on middle for a quick single to mid on.
Similar trajectory, punched straight to cover-point this time by Ali.
Flatter one on off stump, Babar punches it away to sweeper cover for a single and is off the mark.
Four leaves in a row for Azhar. Again wide outside off stump, Azhar lets it go.
Bowls wide outside off stump, the batsman lets it go again.
Again on a good length outside off stump, the batsman lets it go.
Good length delivery outside off stump, Ali lets it go.
Short of a length delivery again, the batsman defends off the back foot.
Short of a length delivery outside off stump, Azhar tries to pull but gets a bottom edge on that one.
Good ball again, on middle. Babar stays back in the crease to defend it.
Flatter one on off stump, Azam defends it on the back foot.

Woah, great ball again! Azam is very lucky as this one bounces a tad too much and turns away to go in between bat and pad. Clips the pad on the way through but the ball is too high and the pad was outside off so there was no chance of an LBW there. The Ultra-Edge shows us that the ball is away from the inside edge too so good decision by the umpire, as well as NZ not to go upstairs.
What a delivery! This full one on off draws Azam forward into a defensive shot and beats his outside edge as it turns away at the final moment.
Looped up outside off, Azam comes ahead and lets it go as it turns away.
Full and flighted on midde, paddled away to deep fine leg by Azhar. The batsmen come back for three.
Ajaz Patel into the attack.
Another bumper, Azam does well to evade it.
There we go, the bouncer follows the full one. Azam ducks under it.
Full and outside off, Azam comes ahead and defends it.
Welcome back. 46 runs needed, 6 wickets in hand. Babar Azam is the new batsman in. And to face.
... Day 4, Session 2 ...

The game though, is firmly in the favor of Pakistan and they just need to play each ball on its merit as they look to go 1-0 up. Just 46 more runs required! On the other hand, if New Zealand manage to get another couple of wickets quickly after the break, the game will open up again. Join us in a while for the post-Lunch session.

The excitement of the first half an hour had been completely blunted by brilliant and patient batting by Asad Shafiq and Azhar Ali. New Zealand were plotting another Pakistan collapse as they managed to pick up three wickets early on but they encountered two rocks in Ali and Shafiq. The hosts' ship sailed clear of troubled waters and reached a very comfortable 130-3 before Wagner played on Shafiq's patience and got him out on the last ball before Lunch.

OUT! No fifty for Shafiq! The barrage of bouncers has done the trick in the end!  This one is on a good length and slightly shaping away and Asad plays a loose shot outside off. The good length ball was only the second one that this bouncer machine, Wagner has bowled today. And it takes the slightest of feathers as Watling gobbles it up at a good height behind the wickets. Shafiq will be kicking himself as he would've liked to finish the game off and we were moments away from the break. With that, it will also be LUNCH on Day 4.
Another bumper on middle, let through again.
No surprises as it's another bouncer outside leg, Shafiq ducks again.
Flighted on off stump, Ali drives to short cover.
Flatter and quicker at the pads, tucked away towards square leg for a couple. Azhar Ali into the 40s now.
Full toss at the pads, Azhar flicks it to short fine leg.
Padded away for the third time in a row as the ball lands well outside leg stump again.
Similar line again, Azhar pads it away again.
Around the wicket and bowled well outside leg, Azhar pads it away.
Oh hello, there we go again. Ends the over with a short one aimed at Shafiq's head. He just ducks again. Quite an exercise. Maiden over.
Finally, this one is on good length and just outside off, Shafiq is forced to play at this one as he drives to cover.
This is getting monotonous now, same delivery and similarly left alone.
Barrage of bouncers here, there is not even a thought of playing at it as Shafiq just lets it go again.
Wagner serving more of the same, Shafiq ducks again.
Short one aimed at the head, Shafiq is content to duck and let it go.
Looped up on off stump, Ali dead bats it.
This one is full and outside off and turning away. Ali pads it away, Sodhi appeals but the ball was well outside off and it was turning away.
Wrong 'un on off stump, Shafiq plays it away to mid-wicket for a single.
Short and outside off, cut away to point.
FOUR! Too full and taken on the full by Shafiq and swept away behind square on the leg side. The deep square leg fielder dives but cannot stop this one. Six away from his half-century.
Looped up outside off, easily driven to sweeper cover for a run.
Six bouncers in the over! Shafiq ducks again and is content to let the ball go through. In no hurry.
Another bumper, Shafiq just ducks and lets it go.
Another short ball on middle, this one doesn't climb as much. Azhar pulls it away to deep fine leg for a single.
Short and outside off, Azhar attempts the pull again, this time in front of square on the leg side. Finds the fielder though.
FOUR! Short again and Azhar is ready this time. Pulls it away behind square leg, always in control and all along the ground for four.
Bouncer first up on middle, Azhar ducks underneath it.
Wagner into the attack now.
Outside off on a length, Ali guides it to sweeper to retain strike.
Wide outside off and turning away, Azhar plays the cut and misses the ball completely.
Short again and pulled away by Shafiq to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Flatter and pitching on leg, Azhar flicks it in front of square on leg for another run.
Short and outside off, cut away to sweeper cover for a run.
Fuller and on off, Asad is well forward in defense.
Sodhi changes ends.
Angling away and well outside off, left alone.
Over the wicket this time, on a good length and off stump line. Azhar is half ahead and defends.
Good length outside off, Azhar is solid in defense.
Full and slower outside off, Shafiq guides it on the front foot to third man for a single.
Slightly fuller and outside off, pushed away through cover-point and comes back for two. Good running that!
Good length outside off, left alone by Asad.

FOUR! Terrific shot. Full and around off, Azhar gets down and sweeps it through mid-wicket for a boundary! 11 from the over, Pakistan pressing on the 'finish-it-quickly' button. 66 more to win. Azhar moves to 30 while the stand is worth 62.
Outside off, played straight to point.
Around off, well blocked out.
Full and around off, watchfully pushed it back to the bowler.

FOUR! And again! This time by a different batsman, for a different result! Pakistan growing in confidence now. Full and outside leg, Azhar brings out the reverse sweep and gets it through point for a boundary!

Aha... innovations coming up now. After a series of blocks and flicks, we now get to see a reverse sweep. Pitched outside leg, helped through third man for three runs. 100 COMES UP FOR PAKISTAN. 74 more needed.
Outside off, left alone.
This time he stays back in his crease and blocks.
Full and just outside off, watchfully pushed out.

A delightful cover drive, finding the gap, keeping the scoreboard ticking and reducing the runs required by 2 more. 50-RUN STAND IS UP BETWEEN THESE TWO. Taken the sting out of the New Zealand attack.
Azhar tries to tap and run towards mid on but realizes that he hit it too well. Sends his partner back.

Good awareness, good batting. Shafiq notices that the fielders on the off side were not quite charging to the ball. Taps this ball with soft hands, just wide of cover and calls his partner through for a quick single. We are getting to that stage where the Black Caps need wickets and that too, in a bunch. 79 more needed now.
Pitched outside leg, Ali pads it away.
That stays low. It is around leg but Azhar manages to keep it out with a back foot defense. That nearly trickled back onto the stumps off the inside edge.
Clips this through mid-wicket for a run.
Comes over the wicket, lands it around middle, watchfully kept out.

FOUR! The partnership continues to grow in confidence. Full on middle, Shafiq comes down the track and whips it over square leg. Acres of free space available in that region. Shafiq has moved to 30 now. His third boundary.
Landed outside of spinning away, punched through point for a single.
A bouncer to end the over, Shaifiq ducks.
Full and just outside off, watchfully defended.
Landed outside off, not played at.
A bouncer on middle, Shafiq ducks.
Landed outside off, steered behind point for a couple.
On a length outside off, well defended.
Goes right back in his crease and defends.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Outside off, a touch too wide, left alone.

4000 TEST RUNS FOR ASAD SHAFIQ! Well played. Important player for Pakistan. Keeps his cool in tough circumstances. Full and around middle, Asad comes down the track and flicks it off the inner half through mid-wicket for a single.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Landed outside off, pushed through point for a single.
On middle and leg, helped through square leg for a run.
The batsman has played it to the point region. They pick up a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a single.
Full and outside off, swinging away, left alone.
Down the leg side, flicked through square leg for a couple.
Trent Boult has been summoned. First over of pace today.

DRINKS BREAK. What an opening hour. Just what a cricket fan would have loved. Three quick wickets, then a partnership following it. It seems like Azhar and Shafiq have eased out proceedings but these are two teams playing in a country where anything is possible any time. You can never rule out a collapse, nor can you avoid a fightback. Hold on to your seats. 95 runs needed, 7 wickets in hand...
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full again, Asad reaches out and drives it back to the bowler.
Around off, pushed back to the bowler.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and outside off, Asad pushes at it with soft hands and gets an outside edge which dies down in front of slip.

FOUR! Second boundary in the space of 3 balls. Short and around off, spinning away, Shafiq rocks back and cut it through point to exploit the massive real estate over there. Punches Azhar's gloves with a smile. This partnership is now worth 33 with Shafiq making 22 of those.
Around off, AA stays back and just about blocks it out.
FOUR! Bad ball and punished. A full toss, on middle, Azhar gets down, reaches out and sweeps it behind square leg for a boundary. The runs required come into double figures now.
Full and outside off, this time Ali reads the hand, comes forward and pushes it back.
There comes the googly, skids on after pitching, Azhar does not pick it at all, playing it from the crease, reading it off the pitch and just about dabbing it towards short leg.
Very full outside off, pretty wide. left alone.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Short and outside off, punched through the covers for a couple.
Full and straight, this time AS comes forward and blocks patiently.
Quicker one, outside off, probably the arm ball, once again Asad wants to drop and run to the off side but Azhar calmly sends him back.
Landed outside off, another push but straight to cover.
Full and outside off, Shafiq taps it to the off side, wants a single but is sent back.
Fuller length this time, watchfully defended.
Another full toss, played with soft hands through mid-wicket for a run.
Much fuller, outside off, spinning away, Shafiq shoulders arms.
Landed outside off, dabbed straight to backward point.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a single.
Full and straight, risky sweep shot employed but the bat meets the ball, getting it to square leg.

NOT OUT. The foot barely moved. Full and outside off, Shafiq came forward to defend but the ball spun away a touch, went past the outside edge and Watling whipped off the bails. The keeper was extremely confident and it was referred upstairs but nothing in the replays.
Is that a stumping? Watling is confident that he has his man. Referred upstairs...

FOUR! Not quite of the middle of the bat but it will do. Full and around middle Shafiq comes down the track and looks to go over the top, but the ball spins in a touch, goes off the inner half, but still eludes mid on.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on.
Short and outside off, spinning away, punched straight to cover.
Full and around middle, driven straight back to the bowler.
A high full toss outside off, Azhar cannot do anything about it, driving the ball straight to short extra cover.
Another single, punched through the covers. Good batting by this pair. They are concentrating on the singles and not just blocking and defending.
Eases this through the covers for a run.
A bit more flight, gets it as a full toss, Shafiq pushes it towards mid on for a quick single.
Outside off, pushed back to the bowler.
Full and outside off, use of the feet from Azhar as he gets to the pitch of the ball and drives it through the covers for a single.
Full and outside off, watchfully kept out.
Goes back and works it through square leg for a single.
Landed outside off, left alone.
Plays this extremely late, off the pitch, waiting for the ball to turn and almost guides it to the men waiting there. Manages to nudge it past first slip for a single.
Short and outside off, punched through cover-point for a couple.
Landed outside off, watchfully pushed back to the bowler.
Full and outside off, eased past cover for a brace.
Landed outside off, a bit too wide, left alone.
Outside off, pushed towards point for a single.
Full and outside off, pushed towards mid off.
Too full outside off, Azhar gets underneath it and drives it through the covers for a single.
Tossed up outside off, watchfully defended.
Down the leg side, Shafiq is drawn forward to flick but misses.
Full again, blocked back to the bowler.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid off.
Better from Asad. Gets to the pitch of the ball and blocks.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended. That nearly went through the gap between bat and pad. Shafiq just about managed to get his bat down in time.
Down the leg side, tucked through square leg for a couple.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for a single.
Landed outside off, let through.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Very full, outside off, Shafiq comes forward but nearly yorks himself. The ball goes back to the bowler.
Full and outside off, driven sweetly but straight to extra cover.
Full and around off, well blocked out.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Fuller and with a bit of extra flight, Azhar defends.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Short and outside off, punched through the covers for a single. 50 UP FOR PAKISTAN. Suddenly, 176 looks like a mountain to climb.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Pushes this through mid on for a run.
Outside off, left alone.
Asad Shafiq walks in at number 5, replacing Sohail.

OUT! Caught and bowled off a full toss! Well, well, well! Are we onto something here? Another soft dismissal. We saw Hafeez chipping one to cover and now Sohail has done something similar. Only the region is different. It is a ball which takes the pitch out of the equation because it does not land at all. Sohail comes down the track but hits it straight back and that too uppishly! Nice catch taken Ish Sodhi, low to his left,. Bang, bang, bang! 3/8 in the span of 8 balls for the Kiwis!
FOUR! Positive cricket. No point in just blocking. Sohail comes down the track gets to the pitch of the ball and whacks it over mid on for a boundary.
Around off, defended from the crease.
Haris Sohail comes in at number 4, replacing Hafeez.

OUT! Chipped straight to cover. Oh wow. One brings two and New Zealand have two new batsmen in the middle. Full and outside off, Hafeez comes down the track and looks to hit it through the off side, but cannot keep it down. He ends up hitting it straight to short extra cover where Colin de Grandhomme makes no mistake. Two wickets in the space of 5 balls for 4 runs!
Ooohhh.... played back from the crease, misreads the line and just about manages to get his bat down in time, to sneak a run through point.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a single.
Full and around off, Azhar brings out the sweep and gets it to fine leg for a couple. FIRST RUNS OFF AJAZ PATEL in this innings.
Azhar Ali comes in at number 3, replacing Imam.

OUT! LBW! First wicket for New Zealand! Imam departs. Beautiful bowling, excellent length. Ajaz keeps persisting on that tight line and is rewarded. Imam was getting frustrated, being unable to work him away and on this particular ball, he was not sure whether to come forward or go back. It is a decision which needs to be taken in a split second and the southpaw is a second late. Costs him. He tries to play that off the pitch, going back and looking to work it to the leg side but misses. Why? Because the ball lands on the rough outside off and the surface explodes. Massive turn and pings the left-hander right in front of middle. No point reviewing that. So. New Zealand have got a wicket early, conceding just 3 runs this morning...
Landed outside off again, a touch quicker, the left-hander gets back and across and defends.
Flighted outside off, Imam comes down the track and pushes it back to the bowler.
Full and around off, well defended.
Full and around off, pushed towards point.
Very full outside off, pushed towards cover.
Full and outside off, the attempted googly, left alone.
A touch short, outside off, spinning in, worked past short leg, towards deep mid-wicket, for a single. The stand is now worth 40.
Full and around off, pushed back to the bowler.
Comes forward and watchfully keeps it out.
Pitched outside leg, Hafeez looks to flick but misses and is hit on the pads. A mild LBW appeal ensues but nothing in it.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Fuller and around off, well blocked out.
Full and around off, watchfully pushed back.
Full and around middle, worked straight to short mid-wicket.
On middle and leg, flicked straight to square leg.

Oohhh.... beaten. Full and outside off, Imam comes down the track, looks to flick, is gone for all money as Watling gets ready to stump. But, the bat comes in the way at the last moment as an inside edge is induced and it hits him on the pads.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Dropped short, stays low, Hafeez adjusts well and pulls it over mid-wicket for a run.
On middle and leg, this time the flick shot is connected, past short leg, for a single.
Down the leg side, Imam looks to flick but the ball goes off his pads to short leg.
Ish Sodhi to bowl from the other end.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
This one spins away, bowled slower through the air, MH looks to defend but gets beaten again.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Comes down the track this time and blasts it straight back. Well stopped by the bowler.
And again! Similar ball, same shot, gets beaten again!
That is a jaffa! Full and outside off, Hafeez comes forward to defend but the ball holds its line and beats the outside edge.
The Kiwis are out in a huddle. The players are out in the middle as well. Ajaz Patel to start off proceedings for the day. Hafeez to face. Here we go...

Danny Morrison has a chat with Neil Wagner. On his achieved milestone of 150 Test wickets, Wagner says that it is something which he doesn't like to think about, focussing mainly on bowling well. On not being given the new ball, Neil says that the team has missed Tim Southee in this Test, going by the horses-for-courses strategy, going in with three spinners. Defends Colin de Grandhomme, stating that he has done well in domestic cricket with the new ball. On himself, he says that he is better with the old ball. Stresses that the game is not over yet and if the Kiwis can manage to get early wickets today, anything is possible. Praises the physio for keeping the guys fit and hopes to keep playing for more time. On him moving to North Island back home, Wagner credits it to Trent Boult and says that it has come across as a great changing factor in his life.
WEATHER REPORT -: It is slightly cloudy out there but there is no forecast of rain. Hopefully we get through the remainder of the game unscathed.

Welcome everyone to Day 4 and what could and should most possibly be the last day of this opening Test. Pakistan are firmly in the driver's seat and the visitors will have to hope for an insane spell from their bowlers to make the hosts sweat as they look to wipe off the remaining 139 runs required. The pitch has eased out and if last evening is anything to go by, the Pakistan openers look more than comfortable out there in the middle. All things said, the odds are stacked firmly in favour of Pakistan taking a 1-0 lead in this three-Test series. Join us for live action in a bit!
... Day 4, Session 1 ...

Another 139 is what is needed and the 'hosts' have 10 wickets in hand. They are outright favorites to take a 1-0 lead. But Pakistan being Pakistan you just never know what to expect of them. Day 4 will most probably be the last day of the Test match and one would expect New Zealand to give it their all. Will there be a surprise in store or will Pakistan continue their dominance? Join us to find out at 1000 local (0600 GMT). Till then, take care and goodbye.

The third session though changed the whole complexion of this game. Yasir Shah and Hasan Ali came to the fore, especially the former. He ran through the middle and lower order and finished with a fifer. Hasan Ali too picked up 5 and the two ensured the lead did not get past 200.

The day began with New Zealand trailing by 18 runs and they were already a wicket down. However, Kane Williamson and Jeet Raval added 86 and took the Kiwis into the lead. Pakistan then fought back as they managed to pick a few wickets quickly but a massive 112-run stand between Nicholls and Watling saw the visitors go on top. The two scored half tons and the Black Caps then, seemed like would stretch their lead to around 250.

Pakistan's session and it is Pakistan's day. First they got the last 6 wickets for 29 runs and then, their openers not only ensured they end Day 3 unscathed but have also deducted 37 runs from the target.
The umpires have offered the batsmen the light and they have taken it. The players are walking off the field and THAT WILL BE STUMPS ON DAY 3!
Shorter delivery on off stump, Hafeez covers the spin on the delivery and defends it with a straight bat.
Flatter and on the pads, Imam flicks to square leg for a single.
Full and overpitched outside off, driven by Imam. A diving Kane at cover stops any runs.

Good ball this! Starts outside off, bounces a lot after landing and hits Imam on the thigh pad and lobs up. Short leg takes it and there is a small appeal but Ian Gould signals to the thigh suggesting it came off the thigh pad.
Fuller and outside off, Imam takes a big stride and defends it.
FOUR BYES! Around the wicket, landing outside off, grips and turns. Beats the keeper and runs down to the fine leg fence for four byes.
Spin from both ends. Ish Sodhi to roll his arm.
Looped up on off, Hafeez defends it coming ahead. Maiden over to start off with for Ajaz.
Full and flighted on off, Hafeez plays it back patiently.
Full and on middle this time, Hafeez defends it straight back to the bowler.
Fuller and on off stump, driven towards mid off.
This ball is on length, Hafeez goes back and keeps it out well in the end.
Looped up outside off, Hafeez plays it with soft hands to point.
Ajaz Patel is into the attack.
The ball was on a length and outside off, Hafeez guides it in the gap to the left of point for a single.

FOUR! Hafeez puts his weight on the front foot and drives it beautifully through the covers for another four! The runs are flowing here. This ball was overpitched and outside off and too easy for the master technician.
Short outside off, Hafeez defends it toward point.
Slightly fuller and on off, Hafeez is half forward and plays it to cover.
Good length on the off stump, Hafeez is solid in defense.
Good length and at a gentle pace but drifting onto the pads, Imam flicks it to deep square leg for a single.
On middle this time, Hafeez stays inside his crease and defends it.
Short of a length and above off stump, Hafeez looks to guide it towards the third man boundary but Grandhomme at gully makes a diving stop.
Wide outside off, Hafeez doesn't need to play at those.
Short of a good length outside off, Imam defends it into the gap on the off side towards cover point again. The batsmen run one.
Outside off on a length, Imam stands tall and defends it to cover point.
Short of a good length and on the pads this time, Imam flicks it away to square leg and comes back for the second. Really good running that!
Around off, Hafeez leans forward and punches it to covers.
Full and around leg, driven back towards the bowler.
Good leave. Very good leave. On a good length on that fourth stump line. Comes back in a bit. Hafeez it all the way through to the keeper.
Outside off again, cut past cover-point for a run.
Length ball outside off, Imam leaves it alone.
FOUR! Edge and away. New Zealand are leaking boundaries. Fuller ball on middle and off. Imam plays across the wrong line. Gets an edge which rolls between the cordon and away to the third man fence.
This is on off, Hafeez is solid in defense.
Angles this into the batter, Hafeez gets behind the line and defends it.
Shortish and on middle, it is worked to mid-wicket.
Pure timing! Not for a boundary but a couple. Hafeez uses the pace of the bowler and then guides it through backward point. They run two.
Good length around off, the batsman guides it towards point.
Fuller in length and outside off, the batsman shoulders arms to it.
On a length and around off, it is blocked.
Once again it is nicely punched but does not find the gap, it goes to the cover-point fielder.
FOUR! Imam looks in great touch out there. Slightly short and outside off, Imam rocks back and slaps it through cover-point. It races away. He is dealing in boundaries at the moment.
Back of a length on middle, Imam defends it onto the ground.
Good length and outside off, the batsman makes a leave.
Full on middle, no swing on offer. It is driven back to the bowler.
Colin de Grandhomme to bowl from the other end.
Back of a length on middle, it is kept out. 11 from the first over, an expensive start by Boult.
Runs again! This is on the pads, Imam flicks it through square leg. They run three. Imam is in the mood to finish it today.
Back of a length on off, Imam pushes it to covers.
FOUR! Take that, says Imam! This is delightful! Full and around off, Imam leans into it, gets right on top of the delivery and strokes it through covers for a boundary. Pakistan off to a flier here.
Good comeback! This is fuller and on the stumps, stays a touch low. Imam pushes it back to the bowler.
FOUR! Cracking start to the Pakistan innings! That has been crunched! Slightly short and outside off, Imam rocks back and punches it through covers for a boundary.
